# Spotlight

Spotlight: a one-step onboarding callout anchored to a `SpotlightTarget`, drawn on `Popover.Positioner` from `@base-ui/react`.

Also asked as: onboarding, feature tour, coach mark, new feature highlight, walkthrough.

**Import:** `import { Spotlight } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.stories.jsx` — Basic, WithMedia, LinkAction, PrimaryAction, SecondaryAction, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, BestPracticesLive, MotionOpenAndClose, MotionReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` + `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Spotlight` to point out one feature the first time someone can use it:
a new button, a changed control, a place to start. It is a single step or a
short, explicit sequence with a `stepCount`, not an ongoing help system.

## Motion

Spotlight reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Each coachmark step is Step. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |

## Alternatives

- For a message that stays in the page until resolved, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a short label on hover or focus over a control, use `Tooltip`.
- For an interactive anchored overlay with arbitrary content, use `Popup`.

## Best practices

### Name the feature, then say what to do. {#name-the-feature-then-say-what-to-do}

A headline names the thing; the body is one sentence.

Do: Short headline, one-sentence body.
Don't: A greeting and a paragraph.

### Show a step count only in a tour. {#show-a-step-count-only-in-a-tour}

One step alone has nothing to count.

Do: Step count in a multi-step tour.
Don't: Step count on a single tip.

### Keep the secondary action quieter than the primary. {#keep-the-secondary-action-quieter-than-the-primary}

The primary action leads as the filled action; the secondary is the outlined one.
Either `SpotlightAction` can take `href` to navigate.

Do: The outlined secondary next to the filled primary.
Don't: Two filled, competing buttons.

### Wrap the target and the spotlight in one `SpotlightProvider`. {#wrap-the-target-and-the-spotlight-in-one-spotlightprovider}

`SpotlightTarget` and `Spotlight` share an anchor through context, so both
need to sit inside the same provider. Pass `target` directly only when the
anchor comes from outside that tree.

```jsx
<SpotlightProvider>
    <SpotlightTarget>
        <Button text="Create" />
    </SpotlightTarget>
    <Spotlight headline="Create a new board" onDismiss={() => setSeen(true)}>
        Start a new board from here.
    </Spotlight>
</SpotlightProvider>
```

### Dismiss it once, and remember that it was seen. {#dismiss-it-once-and-remember-that-it-was-seen}

`isOpen` is yours to control. Store whatever "seen" state applies, such as a
user preference or a session flag, so the same spotlight does not reopen on
every visit.

## Accessibility

- **A dialog, not a tooltip.** The spotlight is a `Popup` with a title and a
  description, read together when it opens.
- **The dismiss control is the first focusable element.** Tab reaches it
  before the body or the actions, so closing never requires finding the
  target again.
- **Escape closes it.** Dismissing with Escape or the close button calls
  `onDismiss`.

## Related

- `Popup`: use when anchoring an overlay dialog or panel to a trigger element.
- `CloseButton`: use when rendering the inverse dismiss control in the spotlight header.

Same group: `Banner` · `Dialog` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage`

## Parts

1. **Target.** `SpotlightTarget` wraps the element the spotlight points at and
   shares its anchor with the `Spotlight` through a `SpotlightProvider`.
2. **Headline.** The dialog title, read first.
3. **Dismiss.** The shared `CloseButton` in its `inverse` tone, in the header, the dialog's first focusable element. `dismissible={false}` leaves it out.
4. **Media.** An optional image above the body.
5. **Body.** The `children` text.
6. **Step count.** A short label like "1 of 3".
7. **Actions.** A secondary and a primary `SpotlightAction`, the secondary first. Each takes `onClick`, or `href` to render a link.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Popup on the brand bold fill with inverse text. |
| Hovered | Dismiss takes the inverse hovered layer. |
| Pressed | Dismiss takes the inverse pressed layer. |
| Focused | Dismiss and actions show the inverse focus ring; see Border. |
| Disabled | Not supported. |
| Dismissed | The popup closes and `onDismiss` fires. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the feature in the headline: "Create a new board". | Write a headline that only says "New". |
| Use one or two short lines in the body. | Explain the whole feature. |
| Label actions with verbs: "Next", "Skip", "Got it". | Use "OK" for every step. |
